summary: You need six graduate lecture courses of at least 3 units each, from CHEM courses numbered above 200 or the approved list from other departments, with at most two outside Chemistry. They must be letter graded with a B or better, and so must CHEM 271 and 273, which only the physical, biophysical and chemical physics concentrations take. CHEM 291 and 299 are required in your first autumn. The audit counts 135 graduate units, research included. You check by hand the 3.0 GPA in lecture courses, the first-year research rotations and joining a lab, continuous CHEM 200 enrollment, the qualifying exam, the third-year seminar and committee meeting, the fourth-year proposal defense, candidacy, the oral exam and the dissertation. A transfer petition can reduce the six courses by up to half; that is moved in by hand.
